core_obligations: Reduction to a good site (proof lines 7565-7569): the companion result allows the author to assume that the site has subcanonical topology and that the sheaf is representable by an object.

Identifications (proof lines 7570-7586): the material on localizations of sites supplies an equivalence between the localized category of sheaves and the slice, together with the identity of the composite with the lower shriek; the author names the inverse functor and records the three resulting identities.

Descriptions (proof lines 7587-7590): the description of the lower shriek follows from the identity of the composite, and the description of the pullback from the computation of the lower shriek of a restriction.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a site with subcanonical topology and a representable sheaf.
Use the equivalence between the localized sheaves and the slice, naming the inverse functor.
Read off the descriptions of the lower shriek and of the pullback.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the slice of a topos over a sheaf is a topos, with a canonical localization morphism whose pullback is the product with the sheaf and whose lower shriek is the forgetful functor (statement lines 7541-7562). The proof is a complete argument: the companion result reduces to a site with subcanonical topology and a representable sheaf (proof lines 7565-7569); the equivalence between the localized category of sheaves and the slice supplies the identifications, with the inverse functor named and the three identities recorded (proof lines 7570-7586); and the two descriptions follow from those identities and from the computation of the lower shriek of a restriction (proof lines 7587-7590). The non-formal content is the reduction and the identifications. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
